chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: The Colored Dixieland Band at the Palais de Hammersmith
summary: Briggs worked in George Mitchell's band at the Hammersmith Palais, a reading and improvising group with erratic drinking players such as the drummer George Hines.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Right. But you weren't in that group. Were you in that group too?
No, I wasn't. I was in another group. That's the Palais de Hammersmith. That's the group that Bechet was in with Benny Peyton.
Yes, the Palais de Hammersmith, a dance place. One of the best.
The funniest thing, is it was owned by an American. Mitchell, George Mitchell, yes.
Yes, George Mitchell. And we had a very fine time. Benny Peyton here and George Mitchell had two of the top shots in this dance place, in Hammersmith. You know Hammersmith?
I don't know whether the Palais still exists, I don't know.
And he had the Rector's Club as well. This was the top shot.
Well, what sort of a group were you in?
I told you, a little while ago. Mr. Mitchell formed our group and called us the Colored Dixieland Band. I told you that -- (Laughter).
We were just called that. That is, there was no proper organization here. We had a wonderful clarinet player.
And our piano player, George Clapham, he was the same way. The drummer, George Hines, -- they are all Georges. George Hines was a wonderful drummer, but not for dancing.
As a showman on the stage or to do a concert, to do tricks, to make people laugh, he was wonderful for that. But not to play tempo in a dance hall.
We had trombone. We had Jacob Patrick, trombone. One of the Syncopated Orchestra. And myself on trumpet.
But you couldn't do everything yourself, you see.
But what were you doing, were these improvise bands or were you reading?
We read and we improvised. Both. We played both.
Oh, yes. We had the talent. The talent was there, but just the men you couldn't count on them, that's all.
Because they were boozing too much?
Yes, too much. And we finished our six months contract and people were not dissatisfied with us, but certain of us were dissatisfied with ourselves, you see.
